name: SOC Capstone Part 1 Detection Coverage & Gap Layer (ATT&CK v19)
description: 10 Active Behavioral Detection Rules across 6 Tactics (Green, Score 100) + 3 Documented Detection Gaps (Red, Score 0).

techniques.comment: Detected by Rule 01: Suspicious PowerShell Execution (EventCode 4688/4104, Sysmon EventID 1)
Detected by Rule 02: Scheduled Task Creation (EventCode 4698 / schtasks.exe)
Detected by Rule 03: Windows Service Creation (EventCode 7045 / 4697 / sc.exe)
Detected by Rule 04: LSASS Memory Credential Dumping (comsvcs.dll MiniDump & Sysmon EventID 10)
Detected by Rule 05: Brute Force Correlation (>=3 EventCode 4625 followed by 4624 within 10m)
Detected by Rule 06: Clear Windows Event Logs (EventCode 1102 / 104 / wevtutil cl)
Detected by Rule 07: Rundll32 System Binary Proxy Execution
Detected by Rule 08: Ingress Tool Transfer via Certutil/Curl + Apache access_combined
Detected by Rule 09: Linux Cron Persistence Modification (auditd key=cron_persistence)
Detected by Rule 10: Linux SSH Authorized Keys Modification (auditd key=ssh_keys)
GAP 1: Process Hollowing — Requires kernel ETW (Threat-Intelligence) or EDR memory inspection beyond standard process creation logs.
GAP 2: LLMNR/NBT-NS Poisoning — Layer 2/3 peer-to-peer broadcast traffic not visible to host-only logs without a SPAN port NDR sensor (Zeek/Suricata).
GAP 3: Kernel-Mode Rootkit (LKM/eBPF) — Subverts ring-0 syscall hooks and suppresses auditd netlink messages before user-space forwarding.
